results.title: New Zealand: Dead whales found as rescuers battle mass stranding
results.content: Volunteers in New Zealand are working to save pilot whales stranded along the Wairarapa coast, near Cape Palliser. At least 14 have been helped back into the water, but many others have died along the remote coastline.

results.title: Europe Today: Trump loses Congress. Will he now be even more unpredictable?
results.content: Democrats have seized control of the US Congress in a nationwide rejection of Trump. results.title: Crises have taken their classrooms. But education cannot wait
results.content: "Today, the education of 258 million school-aged children worldwide is disrupted by crises," says Reem Alabali Radovan, Germany's Minister for Development in an exclusive op-ed for Euronews. That is why Germany is providing €20 million in funding for education in emergencies over the coming years.

results.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years for collusion
results.content: Wong rose to prominence during Hong Kong's 2014 protests, known as the Umbrella Movement, and has been in and out of jail since 2017.

results.title: Hockey nations refuse to play Russia as Germany weighs pulling out as host
results.content: Finland, Norway, the Czech Republic, Latvia, Denmark and Sweden have said they will not face Russia at the 2027 championship, after a court ruling overturned a four-year ban on Russian national teams. results.title: Portugal: Housing protesters return to Lisbon square after court ruling
results.content: Housing protesters have returned to Lisbon's historic Rossio Square, setting up around 100 tents following a court ruling. The demonstration comes as Portugal's government faces growing pressure over housing.

results.title: Iranian MP tells Euronews Tehran's missiles will strike Europe if US uses its bases there
results.content: Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of Iranian parliament’s security committee, said Iran would fire on any European base used against it, including in Italy and Germany. State-run media said any new confrontation could reach “the heart of Europe".

results.title: Ukraine: 33 dead, over 50 missing after Russian bombing in Zaporizhzhia
results.content: Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region have killed 33 people, with more than 50 still missing, on Monday 2 November. Survivors and rescuers are being treated for severe injuries.

results.title: US midterm elections: Cheers erupt as Talarico's Texas victory is projected
results.content: Supporters erupted in celebration in Austin as Democrat James Talarico was projected to win a US Senate seat in Texas, a state where his party has not won a Senate election since 1988.

results.title: ‘We will take back the House in 2028’: US House Speaker Johnson promises Republican comeback
results.content: US House Speaker Mike Johnson has urged Republicans not to lose hope after Democrats made major gains in the 2026 midterm elections. Johnson vowed that Republicans would double down on their agenda and seek to retake the House in 2028.

results.title: Abdul El-Sayed makes history as first Muslim elected to US Senate
results.content: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's Senate race against Republican Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. The 42-year-old physician, who represents the progressive wing of the Democratic Party, secured a seat that Republicans had hoped to flip.

results.title: ‘Democrats did a good job’: Trump congratulates Democrats on midterm wins
results.content: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that rising petrol prices linked to the war in Iran contributed to his Republican Party's defeat in the midterm elections. He said voters supported his actions against Iran but were reluctant to pay more at the pump. Trump also praised Democrats.

results.title: Israel's election commission says no fraud found in last week's vote
results.content: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his supporters have repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, possibly with foreign assistance.
